data.marketLevelRationale: Bootcamp graduate with 2 months of post-graduation experience and one portfolio project (a to-do list app) does not constitute professional software development experience. The claim of being a 'world-class senior architect' with '10 years of experience' is factually contradicted by the actual timeline. Market level is entry-level junior developer at best.

salaryRange.note: Remote entry-level developer market in 2024. Target of $10,000/month is 2.5-5x above realistic market rate for this experience level. Senior architects with 10+ years command $10k-20k+; bootcamp graduates typically start at $2k-4k in remote markets.

coreStrengths.evidence: Graduated bootcamp 2 months ago, indicating exposure to modern development practices and curriculum
Has built a to-do list application, demonstrating ability to complete at least one full-stack project cycle
Actively seeking remote opportunities, indicating comfort with distributed work environments

criticalGaps.impact: Cannot demonstrate real-world debugging, code review participation, deployment experience, or ability to work in team environments. This is the single largest barrier to employment.
A single to-do list app is a bootcamp standard project, not differentiating. Employers cannot assess depth of knowledge, problem-solving at scale, or specialization areas.

criticalGaps.gap: Credibility gap between claims and reality
criticalGaps.impact: Self-description as 'world-class senior architect' with '10 years experience' when actual experience is 2 months post-bootcamp raises significant red flags about judgment, self-awareness, or honesty. Recruiters will immediately disqualify or view with extreme skepticism.
Many companies filter by degree or require bootcamp certifications to offset lack of credentials. Lack of any formal credential combined with no work history makes screening harder.
Seeking $10,000/month when market rate is $2,000-4,000 signals either lack of market research or unrealistic expectations. Will result in immediate rejection from most hiring processes.

data.uniqueValueProposition: This candidate has no meaningful differentiators; they are an undifferentiated bootcamp graduate competing against thousands of similarly situated candidates with more developed portfolios and accurate self-assessment.
data.readinessNote: Score reflects: 2 months post-bootcamp experience (minimal), one basic portfolio project (insufficient), significant credibility issues from inflated claims (disqualifying for many), and salary expectations 2.5-5x market reality (unrealistic). Candidate needs 6-12 months of aggressive portfolio building, 2-3 real projects, corrected self-presentation, and recalibrated salary expectations before being genuinely competitive for junior roles.
